newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NAB's BNZ raises yr net profit by 5.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: NAB's BNZ raises yr net profit by 5.3 pct.

text.p: Bank of New Zealand Ltd, a unit of National Australia Bank, on Thursday reported a 5.3 percent rise in net profit to NZ$318 million for the year to September 30, 1996 from $302 million a year earlier.
BNZ said underlying profit (excluding interest recoveries and before debt provisioning and tax) had risen by 12 percent to $363 million.

Managing Director Gordon Wheaton said: "There has been strong growth in both personal and business markets, with the focus on attracting and retaining quality business. In an environment of tight margins, we have increased our lending
while containing expenses, resulting in a continuing strong profit performance."
Total lending had grown by 10.1 percent to $18.3 billion from $16.6 billion. Home lending was up to $6.3 billion from $5.7 billion a year earlier.

Wheaton said improvements in efficiency and effectiveness, combined with increased levels of business, had contributed to a reduction in the cost/income ratio from 62.5 percent last year to 60.7 percent in 1996.
Recoveries from doubtful debts provided for in previous periods had resulted in a net credit to profit for debt provisioning of $80 million, compared with $103 million in the previous year.
Wheaton said a further reduction in gross non-accrual loans had been achieved from $312 million at September 1995 to $164 million in 1996.
The credits available from recovery of all loans would therefore be at low levels in the next year.
Total balance sheet assets were at $23.5 billion, an increase of $1.6 billion on a year earlier and primarily reflecting a growth in lending.
